description: The 19 distinct muscle_groups strings mapped onto SNOMED CT muscle structures (primary) and, where OPE carries a usable class, onto the NCI Thesaurus classes OPE imports (secondary). SNOMED is primary because it has real functional-group concepts ('Flexor of hip joint', 'Muscle of buttock') that a lay taxonomy actually needs; NCIT is recorded alongside because it is the vocabulary OPE itself speaks.

coverage.snomed: 19 of 19 mapped. 15 skos:exactMatch, 2 skos:broader, 1 skos:closeMatch, 1 skos:narrower pair.

mappings.note: The anatomically correct group concept for the calf: gastrocnemius plus soleus. Preferred over snomed:53840002 'Structure of calf of leg', which is the body region, not the muscle.
Deliberately NOT exactMatch. SNOMED CT has no pectoral group concept; pectoralis major is the dominant but not the only chest muscle. Asserting identity here would quietly drop pectoralis minor.

mappings.target_label: Skeletal muscle structure of chest wall

mappings.note: NCIT beats SNOMED CT here - it has the group concept SNOMED lacks. One of the few places the secondary vocabulary carries the better term.

'Core' is a training-culture term with no clinical referent. It is conventionally taken to include the deep abdominal wall, the diaphragm, the pelvic floor and the spinal stabilisers - a set no single SNOMED concept covers. Mapped broader to the abdominal musculature and flagged, rather than forced.

declined.reason: OPE imports eight individual forearm muscles (Flexor_Carpi_Radialis, Extensor_Carpi_Ulnaris, Pronator_Teres and so on) but no group class above them. Mapping to any one member would misrepresent the catalog term.

mappings.note: A genuine group concept whose children are gluteus maximus, medius, minimus and tensor fasciae latae. SNOMED has no concept literally named 'gluteal muscle structure'; this is it.

Clinically load-bearing for this project: gluteus medius strengthening is first-line conservative management for patellofemoral pain, which is why the contraindication layer promotes hip-abduction work for the sample member rather than merely permitting it.

declined.reason: OPE imports Gluteus_Maximus and Gluteus_Medius as individuals but has no gluteal group class and no Gluteus_Minimus.

mappings.note: Children are biceps femoris, semimembranosus and semitendinosus - exactly the hamstring group.

mappings.target_label: Structure of adductor muscle of hip joint
mappings.note: SNOMED models muscles-acting-on-a-joint as real functional groups. This is the clean win that made SNOMED the primary anatomy vocabulary here - a lay term like 'hip adductors' lands on a first-class concept instead of a hand-rolled bag of muscles.
Narrower than the catalog term - iliopsoas is the principal hip flexor but not the whole group.

mappings.target_label: Structure of muscle of lower back

mappings.note: Narrower - the erectors are the dominant but not the only lower-back muscle.

concepts.disambiguation: This term is also how a coach names a lumbar complaint. When it appears in an injury context it must resolve to snomed:122496007 (Lumbar spine structure) instead. Policy in anatomy-partonomy.json -> ambiguous_surface_forms.

mappings.target_label: Structure of muscle of upper back
mappings.note: The weakest mapping in this file, and kept only for traversal reachability. SNOMED CT partitions back musculature into upper and lower with nothing between; the rhomboids and middle trapezius that a coach means by 'middle back' are classified under upper back. Confidence is low, so this mapping is display-and-traversal only and is never the sole basis for a safety decision.

mappings.target_label: Structure of interscapular region of back
mappings.note: The correct region, but a region concept rather than a muscle concept - so it cannot serve as the primary mapping for a muscle_groups value.

declined.reason: OPE contains no Rhomboid class of any kind and no mid-back group. Nothing to map to.

mappings.target_label: Structure of external oblique abdominal muscle
Structure of obliquus internus abdominis muscle

concepts.notes: No single 'obliques' group concept exists in either vocabulary. Modelled as a narrower pair plus a broader parent rather than picking one of the two and calling it exact. Caution for anyone extending this: NCIT's Superior_Oblique_Muscle and Inferior_Oblique_Muscle are eye muscles.

mappings.note: Also a hip flexor. The partonomy is a DAG here, deliberately.
The muscles-only concept, whose children are supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis. Correct for a muscle_groups value.

mappings.target_label: Structure of rotator cuff including muscles and tendons
mappings.note: Used instead as the anchor for rotator cuff *injury* rules, which are usually tendon pathology rather than muscle pathology.

declined.reason: OPE has no Rotator_Cuff class, and of the four cuff muscles imports only Teres_Minor_Muscle. Supraspinatus, infraspinatus and subscapularis are all absent. Mapping to teres minor alone would be actively misleading.

mappings.target_label: Structure of muscle of upper back

declined.reason: No upper-back muscle group class in OPE. Dorsal_Muscle_of_the_Back is the nearest, but it covers the whole back and would collide with the lower back mapping.

concepts.disambiguation: In an injury context 'upper back' should resolve to snomed:122495006 (Thoracic spine structure). Policy in anatomy-partonomy.json -> ambiguous_surface_forms.

declined_mappings_summary.reason: two members present, no group class
no rhomboid or mid-back class exists at all
no cuff class; 3 of 4 cuff muscles absent
